7c8f1d8a7e.q: Why should designers spend months on brand exploration before committing to a rebrand deadline?
7c8f1d8a7e.a: Alex spent 5-6 months on her rebrand process, with the first 2-3 months in a messy, uncommitted phase where she drew ideas, got feedback, and let concepts evolve before setting a hard deadline. She emphasizes giving yourself time to let ideas be chaotic initially—all within your own head—then moving to phase two where you treat it seriously and set external accountability like telling friends or commissioning collaborators who depend on that deadline.

40eb147295.q: How does hiding behind a studio brand name versus building a personal brand affect client acquisition?
40eb147295.a: Alex spent her first four years of freelancing hiding behind the Dove Branding Co studio brand, telling herself it was a studio model when really she was avoiding showing her personality. She realized her brand wasn't reflecting her properly and dream clients were finding her in spite of her brand, not because of it. Only after recognizing this did she rebrand to something more personal that could evolve with her and better attract aligned clients.

a1cbe4c886.q: Why did Alex Dove choose a monochrome black and white brand identity for four years and what made her change?
a1cbe4c886.a: Alex initially stuck with black and white because she wanted to let her client projects shine and stand out more than her own brand. She now admits she was scared to put more personality out there. After diversifying into paid brand collaborations, Adobe ambassador ambitions, and wanting a stronger personal Instagram presence, she realized her monochrome brand wasn't reflecting her personality at all, prompting the rebrand.

eb5211fc2b.q: What external accountability tactics did Alex Dove use to actually complete her rebrand by deadline?
eb5211fc2b.a: Alex set her rebrand deadline around her birthday and told people she knew would hold her accountable to it. She also commissioned a motion designer to animate her mascot, which forced her to deliver on time because he was relying on her deadline. She arranged a paid brand collaboration that required the rebrand to be finished beforehand. These external pressures transformed the deadline from something only in her head to a hard external commitment.

f1c7a8e289.q: Should designers hire someone else to rebrand them, or should they design their own brand?
f1c7a8e289.a: Alex felt she had to do her rebrand herself because it needs to reflect her and she wouldn't be happy unless she made it, not because she's better than others but because she needed to be in control and ensure it represented everything she does. As a brand designer, her brand is also a representation of her capabilities and style, so outsourcing the main design felt wrong, though she did commission specific collaborators like a motion designer for parts she couldn't do herself.
